neighbours.label: the units a larger body is partitioned into (divisions, companies of a regiment, regiments, sections, provinces, regional governments, tracts); the whole body, or one member of it, stays quiet
fire: The marshal divided his corps into four divisions before the assault.
Three companies of the Second Dragoons were posted along the creek.
Taxes are collected by the central state and by regional governments.
The estate was surveyed and split into sections of one square mile.
The exiles were resettled in several provinces along the frontier.
After the retreat, the scattered regiments regrouped behind the hills.
The reservation was parcelled out in tracts of eighty acres.
The legion marched in separate cohorts along the coastal road.
quiet: The marshal led his corps across the bridge before the assault.
Three officers of the Second Dragoons were posted along the creek.
Taxes are collected by the central state and by nobody else.
The estate was surveyed and sold to a banker from the city.
The exiles were resettled in a valley along the frontier.
After the retreat, the tired general rested behind the hills.
The reservation was fenced with wire and wooden posts.
The legion marched in silence along the coastal road.

notes: Probes: five companies of the Ninth Cavalry 0.52, three divisions 0.47, regional governments 0.35, regiments 0.31, several provinces 0.26; 'his army' 0.06, software companies 0.05. One military 'companies' sentence also stayed at 0.06, so the context matters. The - pole is the other side: per / within / individual (the single unit inside the whole).
